races.name: Party Time And Limerick Motor Centre Rated Race

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been finishing in the frame over 6f on Good ground at the Galway festival, but the Firm going here and a likely single-pace gallop make it hard to see him generating enough momentum from the rear; tongue-tie worn, 7lb claimer Alan Casey aboard, 15 days since last run is fine.|

runners_data.name: Inishfallen
runners_data.note: Stephen Thorne's runner has placed twice at Stables over 6f but has posted 10th and 11th at Galway on recent starts, and a hold-up profile in a race with a sustainable pace leaves him with plenty to find; 3lb claimer Kearney aboard, blinkers on, 14-day turnaround unremarkable.|

runners_data.name: Tokyo Treasure
runners_data.note: 273 days off the track is an immediate flag, and the flagged tendency to fade late in the finish compounds the risk at a distance likely to stretch his reserves on Firm ground; style is unclear (U-tagged), form reads three finishes without a win, and this distance is longer than his best recent efforts at 7f.|

runners_data.name: Clonmacash
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness has an active book of form with 2 wins from 25 runners over 14 days, and this 5-year-old's prominent style is well-suited to tracking the pace on Firm ground; visored, ran 4th at Galway over 6f most recently, and 14 days since last run keeps him fresh for this competitive spot.|

runners_data.name: Send Harry
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, and while a lone front-runner role on Firm ground at 6½f suits the profile, the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) is a mild caution — this horse has more often raced at 7f and a step back in trip with a 7lb claimer could be the one variable; 0 wins from 3 for trainer in 14 days is not encouraging from a stable perspective.|

runners_data.name: Apache Outlaw
runners_data.note: McGuinness runner who is naturally a hold-up horse but is mapped to midfield due to the volume of closers in this field — the redistribution means he is unlikely to get his preferred position at the rear where he operates best; his last two starts over this course and distance were 6th and 11th, and the style constraint limits confidence.|

runners_data.name: Morehampton
runners_data.note: John Murtagh's 3-year-old carries top weight (OR 79) and has a hold-up profile, which is a structural mismatch for a race likely to be run at a modest sustainable tempo; 4 wins from 19 for the trainer in 14 days is a live booking flag, and Rory Mulligan (5) gets a small weight break, but recent form shows a string of double-figure finishes.|

runners_data.name: Western Bandit
runners_data.note: Longer-trip specialist stepping down sharply from 10f — his last three wins or places all came at 10f — and his natural come-from-behind style is further compromised by being mapped away from his preferred rear position due to the cluster of hold-up horses in this field; STYLE_FIT (0.90) and the trip drop make this a difficult assignment.|

runners_data.name: Dancing Saxon
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's 3-year-old returns from a 155-day break off the back of a winning run at Stables over 7f, and a prominent style that allows him to track the pace is ideal for this race shape; the drop to 6½f is a mild query, but Firm ground and a lead horse to aim at could set up a strong run into the home turn.|

runners_data.name: Usuario Amigo
runners_data.note: Poor recent form (9th, 10th, 7th in last three) and a hold-up style that cannot be accommodated at the rear given the density of closers in this field — effectively forced into midfield against his natural preference; OR 64 is the lowest in the race and Jack Cleary (5) cannot fully compensate for structural and form disadvantages.|

runners_data.name: Ocean Echo
runners_data.note: Mark Fahey's 3-year-old is prominent in style and placed at Headford over 7f, giving her a live each-way angle if she can secure a position just behind Send Harry; the step up from 6f to 6½f looks manageable and Gavin Ryan is a strong booking, though her overall form figures (06246) suggest she needs things to fall right.|

races.paceDynamic: Send Harry is the confirmed lone front-runner here, likely to slot straight to the lead from a prominent draw and control tempo on Firm ground over 6½f at Limerick — with no genuine pressure from another natural pace-setter, the fractions should be honest rather than suicidal, creating a rail-hugging gallop that suits those positioned just behind. Clonmacash and Dancing Saxon are the most likely horses to track Send Harry into the race, with Ocean Echo also capable of pressing forward from her prominent profile, giving the front rank a small cluster of challengers. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can absorb at the rear — Apache Outlaw, Western Bandit, and Usuario Amigo are genuine come-from-behind horses who are likely to find themselves shuffled further back than ideal, diluting their finishing impact. On Firm ground at this distance with a single uncontested leader setting a sustainable rhythm, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can slot in behind Send Harry and kick off the home turn, rather than true hold-up horses attempting to close ground they may never fully recover.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Send Harry Controls, Chasers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Send Harry leads cleanly and sets a sustainable Firm-ground gallop with Clonmacash and Dancing Saxon tracking close.
scenarios.body: Send Harry dictates unchallenged, and the honest pace suits horses racing just off the leader who can quicken from the home turn on quick ground; the lack of a pressing rival means the front of the race is not burned out early. Clonmacash and Dancing Saxon are ideally placed to pounce, with the Firm surface rewarding their prominent styles and trainer form solid for both camps.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Two Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Send Harry is pressured earlier than expected by Clonmacash or Ocean Echo, raising the pace fractionally.
scenarios.body: A contested but still measured gallop develops, slightly compressing the field, and the winner is likely drawn from the front two or three who handle the sharper fractions on Firm ground. Dancing Saxon's recent winning form at Stables and Ocean Echo's placed effort at Headford give each a claim if the pace suits a two-furlong dash.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Delivery Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Send Harry sets a genuinely quick gallop early and fades in the closing stages, opening the door for those racing in midfield.
scenarios.body: A fast early pace would compress the finish and allow horses like Alfred Tennyson or Morehampton to close from off the pace if they travel well through the race; Firm going aids those with a clean action who settle and quicken late. However, with no genuine pace pressure on Send Harry expected, this scenario requires a tactical misjudgement from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly strong enough to bring genuine hold-up horses — Apache Outlaw, Western Bandit — into the finish from the rear.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on horses racing well outside their natural position landing in range, which is structurally unlikely given how crowded the back of the field is with hold-up types; Apache Outlaw and Western Bandit would need a contested pace and a clear run through traffic. The probability is materially discounted because both are redistributed from their true style and face an unfavourable race shape.

watchPoints.text: Send Harry's lead is unchallenged but Jimmy Dalton (7lb claimer) is untested in this role — watch for whether he controls the gallop or lets the pace drift too slow, which could compress the finish and bring hold-up horses back into it.

Tokyo Treasure's 273-day absence combined with the flagged fade-in-finish tendency makes her a significant out-of-form runner to track — if she sets off prominently in the early stages she could compromise the race shape for those behind her.

Apache Outlaw and Western Bandit are genuine hold-up horses who will be unable to get their natural rear position given the volume of closers — watch for traffic issues or a wide run late as they seek racing room through a congested field.

Dancing Saxon returns from 155 days off for J P O'Brien and won last time out — stable form is strong (8 wins from 55 in 14 days) and first-time-back winners are worth monitoring from prominent positions in yard like this.|

Morehampton's top-rated OR (79) creates a watch point — if John Murtagh's runner travels smoothly from the rear and the pace is stronger than expected, his class edge could deliver a late run, though the race shape must change significantly for that to materialise.

races.name: Ei Electronics Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner with a recent win over 6f at the Curragh on good; goes on firm, handles the track, and with no rival prepared to seriously challenge for the lead this is a career-best opportunity to dictate from the front — the style-fit flag is worth noting but this trip and surface suit.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose best recent effort was a close second over 7f at the Curragh on good; the step back to 6½f and firm ground is a slight concern for a horse that needs a strong pace to get involved, and blinkers are not listed so no headgear change to sharpen it up.

runners_data.name: Friars Gate
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has been campaigned over 8f on soft and good-to-soft recently, making this trip and the firm surface a notable double concern; finishing fade flag and no wins in five recorded starts over further trips suggest this race shape is unfavourable.

runners_data.name: Undefeatable
runners_data.note: A 260-day absence is a serious flag regardless of ability; won over 6f at Gowran as a juvenile and placed at Sandown, but returning from that layoff into a 17-runner handicap on firm means the stable will likely just want a good run rather than expecting peak performance.

runners_data.name: Notforalongtime
runners_data.note: Veteran of nine who comes into this on the back of a respectable fifth over 8f on good; hold-up style and preference for a longer trip mean this 6½f test on firm ground is probably a furlong short of where this horse is at its best right now.

runners_data.name: Monastere
runners_data.note: Took a 6f Curragh handicap on good in May and followed up with a second, making this horse one of the few hold-up types with genuine course-proximity form; the finishing fade warning is a concern but it is still the most credible closer in the field if the pace ever relents.

runners_data.name: El Fontenaro
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a second over 6f at the Curragh on good last time; versatile enough to sit handy and this 6½f on firm suits — one of the cleanest pace-map fits in the race with Fahey's yard returning a quiet but respectable strike rate.

runners_data.name: Snap Decision
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature who has been placed into midfield on the map due to the volume of closers in this field; recent form shows a string of mid-pack finishes at 7-8f, and stepping back to 6½f on firm with a style-fit discount makes this hard to fancy from a pace-shape perspective — there is a fading pattern in its record too.

runners_data.name: Jazzy Dancer
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has won over 7f at Sligo and placed at Ballinrobe, showing it can get prominent when the draw and pace allow; natural hold-up tendency is squeezed by the volume of closers here, though of the redistributed horses this one has arguably the best tactical flexibility to find a position.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Banter
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed twice over 6f at Sligo on good-to-soft recently; the switch to firm is an unknown but the style fits the likely race shape well, and Kearney's 3lb claim is a useful allowance — trainer Slattery has two winners from 30 runners over 14 days which is modest context.

runners_data.name: Dc Diva
runners_data.note: Limited form over 6-7f on soft and heavy ground, and the switch to firm turf is a significant negative for a hold-up horse that has not run more than three times on record; the finishing fade flag compounds a difficult race shape for this runner.

runners_data.name: Pick A Window
runners_data.note: A finisher who has placed once over 7f on good but whose form string is largely disappointing — the fading tendency, combined with a natural hold-up style being pushed into midfield, means this 6½f firm-ground test is unlikely to see this horse at its best.

runners_data.name: Snowballs
runners_data.note: Placed over 5f on good and good-to-firm at Naas, suggesting the surface is fine, but the step up to 6½f is an unproven trip for a horse whose hold-up style has been redistributed to midfield; hood retained and a 17-day break makes form hard to assess with confidence.

runners_data.name: Hastily
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old who has posted a string of 0s and double-figure finishes, most recently over 5f, 8f and 16f which is a peculiar mix; the style-fit and redistribution flags combine with the fade warning and poor recent form to make this a very tough watch from a pace-map perspective.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a second over 6f on good at the Curragh in recent form; jockey details not confirmed in the entry but the style is right for this race shape and the horse has shown it can be competitive at this level — a legitimate pace-map fit alongside El Fontenaro.

runners_data.name: Gobi Star
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose form is a string of zeros with a best effort of seventh; the redistribution to midfield from a natural hold-up role, combined with the fading tendency and poor recent runs, leaves very little reason to expect a significant improvement here.

runners_data.name: Bel Espoir
runners_data.note: Barcoe's second runner in this race alongside Gobi Star; a four-year-old whose recent form shows a solitary placed effort and mostly mid-to-rear finishes over 5-6f, and the fading flag with a hold-up style mapped to midfield means this horse is swimming against both the pace tide and its own form.

races.paceDynamic: I'm Spartacus is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on firm ground over 6½f at Limerick, should bowl along at a sustainable but honest pace without any serious challenger for the lead — El Fontenaro, Sovereign Banter and Whatswrongnow are the prominent types who will push up behind but none has the profile or inclination to force a pace war. That creates a single-file, controlled tempo where the leader dictates terms from the front and the early fractions are unlikely to be truly testing, meaning the race will be run to suit those able to travel just off the pace rather than deep closers needing a strong gallop. The field contains considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Snap Decision, Jazzy Dancer, Dc Diva, Pick A Window, Snowballs and others are natural hold-up horses who cannot all find genuine cover at the rear and have been redistributed into midfield on the map; of those, Jazzy Dancer and Snap Decision are most likely to get closest to their natural position given their tactical profile and course experience. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers able to sit just behind I'm Spartacus and get a slingshot into the straight — true hold-up horses are disadvantaged by the controlled fractions and will need an unlikely late collapse from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If I'm Spartacus bowls along unchallenged and the pace is steady enough to favour horses tracking just off the leader.
scenarios.body: I'm Spartacus sets a sustainable tempo on the firm ground and horses like El Fontenaro and Sovereign Banter, travelling prominently, are perfectly positioned to pounce in the final two furlongs as the gaps thin; the firm surface rewards those who conserve energy in the first half of the race rather than burning it from the front or from too far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If I'm Spartacus finds the gallop straightforward and its rivals fail to reel it in on the quick ground.
scenarios.body: On firm going over 6½f at Limerick, a horse who gets a soft lead and is not pressed can simply run its rivals into submission, and I'm Spartacus has course-and-distance form to suggest this is a genuine threat; the hold-up horses distributed through midfield will lack the finishing burst needed to bridge a gap if the pace is never truly taxing.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early fractions prove faster than expected and I'm Spartacus and the prominent brigade tie each other up in the straight.
scenarios.body: Only in this scenario do redistributed hold-up types like Jazzy Dancer and Monastere — who has winning form over the course and distance — get an opportunity to close from off the pace; the caveat is that most of the true hold-up horses are running out of their natural position and the pace dynamics make a genuine late collapse unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinders Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes messy with traffic issues mid-pack and prominent horses are checked, allowing a clean run from midfield.
scenarios.body: Horses like Rappell or Notforalongtime, sitting in the slipstream and finding a clear passage, could theoretically pick up the pieces if the stands-rail group stacks up; however, the firm ground does not genuinely suit deep closers and the style-fit concerns for most redistributed horses make this the least likely shape to deliver a winner from the rear.

watchPoints.text: I'm Spartacus receives an uncontested lead on firm ground — if no horse moves to press it through the early stages, watch for Sovereign Banter and El Fontenaro to be the most dangerous chasers into the straight.

The volume of redistributed hold-up horses crowding into the midfield section creates a real risk of traffic problems in the straight — Snap Decision, Dc Diva and Pick A Window in particular may find gaps closing in a 17-runner field on a flat track.

Undefeatable has not run for 260 days; even if it retains ability, horses returning from long breaks in big-field sprint handicaps frequently need the race and could be a drifting market indicator worth watching in early shows.

Monastere is the one hold-up horse with genuine recent course-proximity form (won and placed at 6f on good at the Curragh) — if the pace does fold in the final furlong it is the most likely beneficiary of any late surge despite the fade flag.

Firm ground is consistent across all Limerick races today; no horse flagged with a going concern, but those with exclusively soft/heavy wins in their history (Dc Diva) may find the surface quicker than ideal.

races.name: DAR Golf And Mann Family Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Zheleznaya Dama
runners_data.note: Shane Kelly rides a hold-up filly with a notable tendency to fade late, and her recent form at The Curragh over 7f on good-to-firm shows no winning thread; stepping back to 6½f may help but the finishing frailty is a real concern on fast ground.

runners_data.name: Baby Basma
runners_data.note: Gavin Ryan picks up the mount on a filly whose sole win came over 5f at Gowran on good-to-firm, and 79 days off the track at 3 is not ideal; the shorter trip here and firm going suit the profile better than her recent 6f placed efforts suggest.

runners_data.name: Princess Chloe
runners_data.note: A 134-day absence is the dominant concern here, though the tongue-tie is retained and Jessica O'Gorman claims 7lb; hold-up style from a yard operating at 1 from 4 over the last fortnight, and a 7f/5f form profile that may not pin down this 6½f trip.

runners_data.name: Spirit Above
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle rides a hold-up 3yo who ran second over 5f on good at The Curragh 22 days ago, and the step up to 6½f on firmer ground is a modest risk; tongue-tie and pads suggest a free-going tendency that McMonagle will need to manage smartly.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who has been pushed into midfield on the map because the rear of this field is overcrowded; all five career runs have come over 8f or further at The Curragh and Leopardstown, making this drop to 6½f on firm ground a sharp question about her stamina profile in reverse.

runners_data.name: Jampa Ling
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and a critical pace-shaping figure; STYLE_FIT flags a mild out-of-role concern, but in practical terms he simply leads — three of his last four came over 6f at The Curragh and the switch to Limerick's right-hand track and firmer ground requires watching closely.

runners_data.name: Sayonara
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's in-form yard (5/36 last 14 days) is the angle here, but Sayonara is a genuine hold-up filly repositioned to midfield because the hold-up section is oversubscribed; her best effort was 3rd over 6f at Slane on standard and stepping to 6½f on firm is unproven.

runners_data.name: Ochtar Againn
runners_data.note: Carries headgear (p) and a fade-at-finish flag, and is a true hold-up type shifted forward on the map purely by the density of closers in this field; five runs without a win, largely over 8f-10f at The Curragh, raise real questions about whether 6½f firm is her game.

runners_data.name: Dialin For Dollars
runners_data.note: 282 days off the track is the glaring flag for David Marnane's 2yo (now 3yo), and her form shows a 3rd over 6f at Goodwood as the career highlight; held up naturally but shown in midfield by redistribution, this is a fitness-first query rather than a race-shape one.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: Patrick Magee's consistent sort has run 2nd twice over 6f at The Curragh on good and was placed again 10 days ago; prominent style (tp) makes him the most natural stablemate to Jampa Ling in terms of race position and his chance depends largely on pressing the front-runner into a contested early tempo.

runners_data.name: He's Holding Court
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's second runner carries a fade flag and is a confirmed hold-up type placed in midfield only because the rear section is full; five runs over 8f at The Curragh with a best of 4th suggests this 6½f firm test is sharply outside his comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Windsor Lily
runners_data.note: Wears blinkers and shows a consistent fade pattern, with a career-best 5th over 6f at Slane on standard; a natural hold-up type bumped to midfield by field overcrowding, and 38 days off the track with no firm-ground win adds to the query.

runners_data.name: Iryna's Star
runners_data.note: Terry Casey claims 7lb for Michael Mulvany, who has one winner from 13 runners in the last fortnight; 67 days since last run, a fade flag, and all recent form on soft-to-good suggest firm ground at 6½f is a step into the unknown — holds up naturally but is mapped to midfield by redistribution pressure.

runners_data.name: Sand Art
runners_data.note: Kevin Thomas Coleman's filly has run exclusively over 7f-10f in her last four outings, making this drop to 6½f on firm ground a potentially sharp trip reduction; a hold-up type placed in midfield by redistribution, she carries no meaningful recent form at this distance or going.

runners_data.name: She's On The Ball
runners_data.note: Laura Hourigan's filly has a form string of five poor recent efforts (best a 5th) and no jockey listed — a data flag worth noting; hold-up style placed into midfield by overcrowding, and all career form comes on good or softer, making firm ground an untested variable.

races.paceDynamic: Jampa Ling is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner 0-60 handicap over 6½f at Limerick on firm ground, and with no meaningful challenger for the lead, Scott McCullagh can dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from the front. Glen Breeze is the only other prominent-profile runner likely to press into the first two or three positions, leaving the remainder of the field — including Sayonara, Dawn Flame, Ochtar Againn, Dialin For Dollars, He's Holding Court and Windsor Lily — shuffled into midfield or further back despite being natural hold-up types who cannot all reach their preferred position. On firm ground over 6½f with a soft, unhurried early pace set by a single front-runner, the race will be run at a tempo that conserves energy and rewards those who can switch off and travel close enough to deliver at the two-furlong pole. The tactical verdict is clear: horses racing prominently or within two to three lengths of Jampa Ling into the straight will have the decisive positional advantage — true closers running from their natural far-back position face an uphill task against a pace that will not blow up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jampa Ling Leads Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Jampa Ling settles into an uncontested front-running role and Glen Breeze tracks in second without applying pressure.
scenarios.body: Jampa Ling controls every yard, the pace is moderate on firm ground and nothing lands a blow from behind; the horses who travel prominently and conserve energy for a sustained finish are perfectly placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Glen Breeze presses Jampa Ling from early, lifting the tempo to a genuinely even pace that sets up a two-horse duel.
scenarios.body: A contested lead burns off Jampa Ling late and gives a well-positioned midfield horse the opportunity to deliver on the outer; those with a little more finishing kick over 6½f on fast ground benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Make Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely collapses in the final furlong and the field compresses, allowing the hold-up horses who have tracked close enough to pounce.
scenarios.body: Even redistributed hold-up types who have managed to sit three or four lengths off the pace in midfield could reach a tiring leader; only those with solid firm-ground form have realistic claims given the majority are racing out of role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Spreads
scenarios.trigger: If the early moderate pace sees a chaotic final two furlongs with runners fanning wide and the form-book thrown out.
scenarios.body: Low-rated runners with fresh legs and a clear run find gaps as the tired pace-setters unravel; unexposed or lightly-raced types with decent firm-ground action could outrun their odds.

watchPoints.text: Jampa Ling sets the entire pace dynamic — if Scott McCullagh gets a clean break from the gates and establishes an uncontested lead within the first furlong, the race is effectively run to his tempo and anything behind him is chasing a moving target on firm ground.

Glen Breeze is the only horse with the prominent profile to challenge Jampa Ling for early position; if J M Sheridan attacks from stall draw and applies pressure from the outset, the moderate pace scenario evaporates and the race shape changes materially.

The field holds at least nine confirmed hold-up types all competing for fewer than three viable close-up positions; horses like Sayonara, Dawn Flame and Ochtar Againn are unlikely to access their natural running style and punters should not assume they will race from where the map places them.

Firm ground at Limerick throughout the card is consistent and well-established; any horse whose best form has come on soft or standard (notably Dawn Flame, Ochtar Againn, Iryna's Star) faces an unambiguous going concern that the form figures alone do not fully capture.

Several runners are 10-11 days since their last run and return quickly — Glen Breeze, Dawn Flame, He's Holding Court and She's On The Ball all fit this profile; on firm ground with a compressed field this could accelerate any fatigue in the final furlong.

races.name: Conference & Banqueting Facilities At Limerick Median Auction Fillies Maiden
Panoramic Restaurant At Limerick Racecourse Apprentice Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Young Churchill
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who has been out 103 days and lacks recent fitness, running over a trip that stretches his best form; going is fine but his last few runs at 10f or further show no consistency, and his return from a long absence is a significant negative.

runners_data.name: God Of Thunder
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse running for Denis Hogan who has been placed once in five recent starts at Goodwood over 12-13f; headgear (tongue-strap, cheekpieces) is engaged and the firmer ground is a slight question but the trip suits his stamina profile.

runners_data.name: Grey Fable
runners_data.note: Won over 12f at Standside on similar underfoot conditions and has placed prominently at 15f on good ground; a natural hold-up performer but one with the class and distance aptitude to make a late, meaningful move, and the 21-day break keeps freshness on his side.

runners_data.name: She's Ideal
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who sets the entire race shape; OR 56 with a claimer aboard, she has been running over shorter (9-10f) so the 1m4½f trip is untested, and she is technically racing out of her usual role given the prominent tagging versus field dynamics — the trip stamina question is the key risk to her control.

runners_data.name: Faerie Tales
runners_data.note: Has faded in finishes and shown very little in three runs, all on good or faster ground at Goodwood; a true hold-up type who is now displaced towards midfield by the weight of closers in this field, and the sparse and unencouraging form string makes her difficult to recommend.

runners_data.name: Metamorpheus
runners_data.note: Demonstrated real ability with a win on soft at 10f and placed efforts at 16-18f, making this trip a genuine fit; by nature a horse that wants to be held up, he is pushed into a midfield position by the crowd of hold-up types, so a clean passage will be essential if his finishing kick is to land.

runners_data.name: Magna Gee Gee
runners_data.note: Has placed at 12f on good ground suggesting a modest level of competence, but a poor recent record (0,7,0,8,6) and a 4-year-old apprentice-ridden profile make this a speculative each-way proposition; holds up naturally but is displaced into midfield by the field's structural crowd.

runners_data.name: Eye Contact
runners_data.note: An extended absence of 282 days (since last run, jump start) is a glaring fitness concern; a hold-up horse whose last meaningful effort was 6th over 19f on good at Galway, and the cheekpieces are noted — raw fitness must be the doubt here.

runners_data.name: Deluca Chop
runners_data.note: The form book reads encouragingly with three wins and three places from his last six runs including wins at 13f on soft and good, making this a strong fit on paper; runs prominently, which is a key tactical advantage in this race shape where he can track She's Ideal and produce a natural kick — visor retained throughout the sequence.

runners_data.name: Without Love
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type with a recent run eight days ago and a win at 10f on standard at Standside; displaced into midfield mapping, though capable of a forward move from there given recent fitness, and the quick turnaround from last week is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Cuckaloo Hill
runners_data.note: Has shown a tendency to fade in finishes and her form string is all figures (0,4,0,0,5) with no wins at this sort of distance; 19 days since last run is fine, but she is a redistributed hold-up type with no strong angle and no evidence of handling this sort of stamina test.

runners_data.name: Ravens Can Fly
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old with only three career runs and a modest form line (0,0,4), facing an 14-runner handicap at 1m4½f on firm ground; fades in finishes and is a hold-up type who will struggle for position in this crowded field — Andrew Slattery has a decent recent strike rate but the inexperience here is significant.

runners_data.name: Hosanna Power
runners_data.note: A 6-year-old who ran 79 in recent form at 10f on good, suggesting a modest level, and is a natural hold-up performer; 44-day break, cheekpieces (tp noted), and a low OR of 45 mean she occupies the bottom end of the market logic — form on shorter trips reduces confidence at this distance.

runners_data.name: Lady Luck
runners_data.note: Fades in finishes and has a consistent record of mid-to-rear placings across 8-12f on various surfaces; 53-day absence and a tongue-tie noted, while the redistribution into midfield from her natural hold-up role reduces the likelihood she secures a clean, race-winning run.

races.paceDynamic: She's Ideal is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner apprentice handicap over 1m4½f on firm ground at Limerick, and with no genuine challenger to her lead, she is set to control proceedings at a sustainable, unforced gallop that keeps the tempo honest rather than scorching. Deluca Chop is the only other horse with prominent tendencies and will likely track She's Ideal into second or third, leaving the remainder of the field — a mass of natural hold-up types — competing for midfield positions in what becomes a bunched and tactical procession. On firm ground over this trip with a lone, uncontested pace-setter dictating a measured gallop, the race shape strongly favours horses who can race close to the pace or make a smooth, well-timed move from a prominent position rather than closing from the rear. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the back: Metamorpheus, Magna Gee Gee, Faerie Tales, Eye Contact and Without Love are among those whose natural rearward position will be compromised, with Deluca Chop and Grey Fable best placed to exploit the controlled tempo from close to the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: She's Ideal Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If She's Ideal sets a comfortable, unchallenged gallop that she can sustain through the final two furlongs on this firm surface.
scenarios.body: She's Ideal dictates every fraction from the front and, with no rival willing to press her, produces a measured pace that plays to her strengths over this trip; firm ground suits and a 7lb claimer in Sadhbh Tormey keeps the weight manageable.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If She's Ideal's early control sets up a falsely slow pace that allows a prominent tracker to coast into a decisive lead turning for home.
scenarios.body: Deluca Chop has shown consistent form placing in handicaps at similar distances and thrives on a sound surface, sitting just off the pace and kicking at the optimal moment; Grey Fable won over 12f at Standside on a sound surface and should be travelling well enough to challenge from second or third.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight leaving a gap for a genuine hold-up horse to pick off tiring leaders in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Metamorpheus showed a recent course-and-distance win at 10f on soft and has the class to finish off a race, but is compromised by the crowded hold-up profile meaning clean air may not arrive in time; God Of Thunder and Young Churchill are seasoned hold-up performers who could benefit if the front horses stop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If She's Ideal's early exertions on firm ground cause her to capitulate, triggering a bunched and chaotic finish with no dominant winner.
scenarios.body: A slow crawl followed by a sudden mid-race sprint fractures the field and brings multiple hold-up horses into contention simultaneously; however, the redistributed nature of most closers in this field means their true position will be compromised and the resultant winner is likely to emerge from midfield rather than the rear.

watchPoints.text: She's Ideal's stamina over 1m4½f is unproven — all her form is over 9-10f, and if she ties up in the straight the entire race shape collapses and anything prominent behind her becomes the race.

Deluca Chop's consistent placing record (233211) is the standout form in the race and he must be watched closely tracking the leader, especially if She's Ideal sets a tempo that flatters horses with a prominent kick.
Eye Contact's absence of 282 days (jump start) means fitness is a major unknown — watch the paddock and market closely before drawing conclusions about her chances.

The sheer volume of hold-up types displaced into midfield (Metamorpheus, Magna Gee Gee, Without Love, Faerie Tales) creates a risk of serious traffic problems in the straight — any of these winning will require a clear, unobstructed run.

Grey Fable won over 12f on a sound surface at Standside recently and holds natural hold-up ability with the class to deliver a late challenge — watch his position turning for home as a guide to whether the pace scenario has been truly falsely run.

races.name: Private Suites At Limerick Racecourse Handicap

runners_data.name: Themis
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead-trained hold-up performer returning in 22 days with a win over 12f in soft at Leopardstown as best form, but the firm going and a flagged tendency to fade in the finish are genuine concerns over this trip at Limerick.

runners_data.name: Bell Ex Too
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this hold-up type for R P Cody, who is in modest form at 2/4 over 14 days; all recent runs have been at 10-12f and the step to 1m4½f on firm is untested, but the style matches a well-run race if one materialises.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Drills
runners_data.note: Bolger's representative with an unclassified style ridden by Nathan Crosse, whose trainer is 1/8 over 14 days; has run respectably at 10f on soft and good, and the step to 1m4½f on firm is the key question mark, but versatility in position could be an asset.

runners_data.name: Hassaniya
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner in this field, which hands her an uncontested lead on firm ground; the STYLE_FIT tag signals she is racing somewhat outside her optimal profile as a prominent type pushed to lead, but the absence of any rival to press her means she can dictate entirely on her own terms.

runners_data.name: Maxminelli
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead sends out this unclassified type wearing a tongue-tie, returning after 43 days; recent form includes a third and a second at 10f on good, suggesting stamina for this trip, and the longer absence warrants monitoring but the trainer is in strong form at 11/33 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Lamberella
runners_data.note: David Marnane's runner is a genuine hold-up type carrying a REDISTRIBUTED tag — placed in midfield on the map purely because more hold-up horses exist than rear slots allow — and also wears a tongue-tie; a STYLE_FIT caution applies given this forced positional compromise, and recent form figures of 0-9580 inspire little confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Hassaniya is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to control proceedings at a measured, uncontested gallop over this 1m4½f on firm ground at Limerick. That lack of pressure means the pace is likely to be sustainable rather than searching, with Hassaniya able to dictate tempo from the front without being harassed into burning out her rivals. The hold-up brigade — Themis, Bell Ex Too, and the redistributed Lamberella — will be tracking from the rear, but on a flat course where a controlled pace rarely sees a true end-to-end test, those who can sit in behind and produce a sustained finish from mid-race are best placed. Lamberella, though a natural hold-up type, has been mapped to midfield because this field contains more hold-up runners than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, and Hassaniya is the horse most certain to secure her natural front position. The race shape favours a prominent or mid-division horse who can travel economically in behind the leader and pick up when the tempo lifts in the straight — pure hold-up horses reliant on a strong pace being set face a more uncertain environment here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hassaniya Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hassaniya dictates a steady-to-moderate pace throughout and the field fails to mount a serious challenge until the straight.
scenarios.body: Hassaniya slips into a comfortable rhythm on the lead with Gaelic Drills or Maxminelli tracking in proximity, and any hold-up horses find themselves with too little late pace to reel in a front-runner who has conserved energy through a falsely run race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mid-Division Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just brisk enough to stretch Hassaniya and a mid-division horse picks up powerfully in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A slightly quicker early tempo from Hassaniya strings out the field and leaves room for Maxminelli or Gaelic Drills, tracking in the first two behind the leader, to pounce on a tiring front-runner inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If Hassaniya sets a genuinely testing pace and the closers find sufficient room and momentum to swoop late.
scenarios.body: Themis or Bell Ex Too benefit from a well-run race that stretches the field, getting a clear run to deliver their finishing effort on firm ground over a trip that could suit; however, both flag as faders in the finish, limiting confidence in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Flat-Footed Upset
scenarios.trigger: If Hassaniya weakens dramatically after setting pace and a runner switches wide to deliver an unexpected burst in the straight.
scenarios.body: An unlikely but possible scenario where Gaelic Drills, whose style is unclassified and who has shown versatility in placement, capitalises on a field that collapses around a spent leader.

watchPoints.text: Hassaniya — watch whether she is allowed to stride entirely unchallenged in the early stages; if she dictates without any pressure this race shape almost entirely belongs to her and horses that need a strong pace to deliver their finish are in serious trouble.

Lamberella — mapped to midfield but is a natural hold-up runner; if she is pushed up by her jockey trying to reclaim a natural position, it could create a pocket of unexpected pace in the mid-division that unsettles the race rhythm.

Themis and Bell Ex Too — both flagged as hold-up types who fade in the finish; if the pace is modest as expected, neither may get the strong end-to-end gallop needed to launch a meaningful late challenge, making their closing style a handicap rather than an asset.

Maxminelli — the 43-day absence for a De Bromhead yard in solid 14-day form is worth tracking; horses returning here after a break on firm ground at this trip can either strip fit or come up short, and the market move or drift at the off will be informative.
